We don't need this. I think we can just use getter memorySizeInKB and then convert the units yourself where needed.
Done, thanks.

Consider register_property_r with a custom getter that reads from memorySizeInKB. 
The benefit isn't memory, but a single source of truth — the D-Bus cache and the member can never drift out of sync because the getter recomputes on every read. 
Ref: 
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/90189/2/src/nvidia-gpu/Inventory.hpp
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/90189/2/src/nvidia-gpu/Inventory.cpp
Done, thanks.

This duplicates the long-running pipeline boilerplate shared with NvidiaGpuCurrentUtilization and NvidiaGpuEccMode. 
Please refactoring to use the NvidiaGpuLongRunningCommand helper proposed in
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/90492 once it lands.
Thanks!
Thanks, I will wait for 90492 merge than I will refactor base on 90492.

Done, thanks.

nit: This nests one level deeper than NvidiaGpuCurrentUtilization
(`processor_bandwidth` is flat under gpu_<name>). Is the extra `memory/`
intentional for future grouping with other memory metrics, or should it
be flattened to `memory_capacity_utilization` for consistency?
Done, thanks.
Don't think this is necessary we can use plain set_property call to update the value on dbus and that way dramItemIface can be created and populated in GPU Device class.
Done,thanks.

Sharing the class instance across different classes should be handled carefully.
In your case, you were sharing `inventory*` to `dramItemIface` while they were all attributes of `GpuDevices`. 
Having destructor of `GpuDevices` on flight while having user trying to access this property published on dbus will resulting in daemon crash, because `inventory` will have been destroyed while `dramItemIface` isn't(which means user can still found the interface and property online).
Done,thanks.
Let's store the value in member data in same unit that we have received it with MCTP VDM command.
Done,thanks.

Noticed that `dramItemInterface` is declared earlier than `inventory`, which means
`inventory` will be destroyer earlier in a reverse manner.
Done,thanks.
`inventory` is the very last few attribute in `GpuDevices`.
Done,thanks.
We can avoid this check since we already have check while updating the value on dbus.
Done,thanks.
Due to the same reason, we should at least have a checker before accessing to `inventory`.
Done,thanks.
